dedupe_keys.name: non synthetic european low voltage test system

description: This data set is a standard low-voltage test network built from real utility data, not a synthetic design. It was published on Mendeley Data in May 2019 by Pablo Arboleya, Arpan Koirala, Lucía Suárez-Ramón and Bassam Mohamed. The motive is that standard test systems are central to testing algorithms, operation procedures and planning, and smart meter roll-out changed distribution systems, so a realistic test case with measured loads was needed. The network was taken from the utility's geographical information system and combined with smart meter readings. It represents a real European urban low-voltage distribution network with 10,290 nodes, 8,087 customers, 1,138 supply points, 136 fuses or breakers and 30 power transformers. The package includes the raw GIS and smart meter data and MATLAB functions that build the OpenDSS model, load it with 20 days of measured demand and solve the power flow. It is downloadable from Mendeley Data under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: the page does not name the city or utility, and the measured period is only 20 days. Simulation uses are low-voltage power flow, hosting capacity and smart meter analytics. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
